stars.why: Houston is down to its thinnest backcourt of the season at Washington: Fred VanVleet is ruled out on the first night of a back-to-back and Marcus Smart is still suspended, so more of the offense runs through Sengun. Clint Capela is still out and Steven Adams is only probable in his return, and Sengun has played 37 minutes in each of his last two games.

Oklahoma City is still without Chet Holmgren, Jalen Williams, Cason Wallace and Jaylin Williams, and Ajay Mitchell is questionable with a left ankle sprain, so Gilgeous-Alexander carries nearly all of the creation. Defenses have keyed on him with the roster this thin, and he played 39 minutes in Friday's one-point loss to the Clippers.

Boston hosts a Dallas team on the second night of a back-to-back after Kyrie Irving played 37 minutes at Cleveland on Saturday. Tatum leads Boston in every category and played 38 minutes in his last game; Dallas has not posted its injury report yet.

Atlanta is without Kingston Flemings (lumbar strain), Asa Newell and Mouhamed Gueye at Milwaukee, and Johnson's on-ball share is already up this season. He played 40 minutes Friday and is projected for his normal starting load. His game has a 234.5-point total.

Sacramento's lead guard has played at least 33 minutes in each of his last four games, and Maxime Raynaud remains out. Keegan Murray (illness) and Precious Achiuwa (left ankle soreness) are both questionable against Oklahoma City, which could push even more usage his way.

scrubs.why: Fred VanVleet is ruled out and Marcus Smart is still suspended, so Sheppard is projected to start at Washington after playing 17 to 20 minutes off the bench in his last three games. He went scoreless Friday, but the open guard minutes are the reason to play him, not the last box score.

Kingston Flemings, who started Friday, is out with a lumbar strain, which opens starting minutes on the wing. Dort started three games earlier this month when Jalen Johnson was out, and he went back to about 20 minutes off the bench once the lineup was healthy. His game has a 234.5-point total.

scrubs.note: Moved toward his recent minutes (24.7 a game).
scrubs.why: Alex Sarr (illness) and Tre Johnson (low back soreness) are both questionable against Houston, and either absence pushes Coulibaly's minutes up. He has played 25 and 29 minutes off the bench in his last two games, and his value comes from steals and blocks more than scoring.

Houston has no Fred VanVleet tonight and no Marcus Smart (suspension), so Bogdanovic is one of the few guards left behind Reed Sheppard. He has played 10 to 12 minutes in his recent games, so this is a role bump on paper, not a proven one.

scrubs.note: Moved toward his recent minutes (24.7 a game).
scrubs.why: McBride has played 22 to 27 minutes off the bench in New York's last three games, a steady rotation role rather than a spot fill-in. Toronto is without Kawhi Leonard, and Scottie Barnes is questionable with a left groin strain.

scrubs.note: Moved toward his recent minutes (20.0 a game).
scrubs.why: Dallas is on the second night of a back-to-back at Boston, and Kyrie Irving played 37 minutes Saturday, so watch whether Dallas eases Irving's load. Clayton played only 13 minutes Saturday with Irving on the floor that long; Dallas has not posted its injury report yet.

Adams is probable to return at Washington from a right soleus strain that has kept him to one game this season. Clint Capela is still out, so Houston needs a backup center behind Alperen Sengun, but his first game back may come with limited minutes.

scrubs.note: Moved toward his recent minutes (14.0 a game).
scrubs.why: Sacramento's bench minutes for Monk have swung from 3 to 21 in his last four games, which is the risk. Keegan Murray and Precious Achiuwa are questionable and Maxime Raynaud is out, which is the reason he could see the higher end of that range against Oklahoma City.

guide: Pair two or three stars with two or three scrubs, then fill the middle. The scrubs are what make the stars fit under the $50,000 cap.
